items.title: Deploy the AI gateway with virtual keys, encrypted key storage and the metering bridge
items.outcome: A gateway runs inside the private network, provisions a per-user virtual key bound to that user's entitlement, stores any user-supplied provider key under envelope encryption that never appears in a log, and consumes the quota primitive rather than counting for itself.
items.context: All model traffic routes through the backend by decision, so the gateway is the single choke point for cost, audit and isolation. Key material is the highest-value secret in the system and the documented failure mode is that it ends up in a trace or a log rather than in an attacker's hands directly The gateway depends on the published quota contract rather than on the billing implementation: the contract is the freeze point, so gateway development proceeds against the contract and a mock while production enablement stays gated on real metering.
scope: Gateway deployed on the chosen runtime, reachable only from within the private network
Per-user virtual key carrying the plan budget, model allowlist and rate limits
Key updates on plan change and revocation on downgrade
Envelope-encrypted storage of user-supplied provider keys with memory clearing after use
Redaction guarantees so no key appears in any log, trace or error
Reserve, stream and reconcile bridge to the published quota primitive
Namespacing so one user's context cannot reach another's
Authenticated workload identity and delegated user context on every gateway call
User-initiated provider-key replacement and revocation with no plaintext recovery path
Fresh phishing-resistant step-up assertion for every key add or replacement, with immediate revocation requiring no cooling delay
Pending activation and cancellation for a change made after recovery, on an untrusted device or under a takeover signal, with a twenty-four-hour cooling period and verified-channel notification
Automatic suspension of every stored user-provider credential when account recovery or credential reset completes
Consumes the generated Python client from the contracts pipeline rather than a hand-written HTTP shim
acceptance_criteria: The gateway is unreachable from the public internet, proven by an external connection attempt
A user's virtual key reflects their entitlement and changes within the published time on a plan change
No key material appears in logs, traces or error output, proven by a log scan test with a planted key
Streamed consumption reconciles exactly against the reservation and a failed reconciliation never charges the user
A cross-user context bleed attempt fails; cache and session keys are namespaced by user
Every key decryption is audited
An unauthenticated workload, wrong audience or forged delegated subject is rejected before provider routing
Replacing or revoking a provider key invalidates cached material within the published time and leaves no old key usable
A stale or absent step-up assertion cannot add or replace a provider key, and the refusal reveals no key state
A high-risk key change remains unusable for twenty-four hours, is visible as pending, can be cancelled from the notification link and never becomes active after account recovery suspends it
Account recovery suspends existing provider keys before a recovered session can invoke a model; re-enrollment requires a new step-up
The gateway calls the api only through the generated Python client, and a hand-written request path to a contracted endpoint fails review
Every monetary value the gateway handles is the Decimal-backed Python money wrapper defined by T-ADR-MONEY-01; a float amount fails a test
contracts_schema: Consumes the published quota contract; the gateway holds no authoritative counter
Depends on the published Python client and its contract verification, so a contract change reaches the ai-service as a regeneration rather than a manual edit
security_privacy: User-supplied keys are encrypted with per-user keys and are never returned by any endpoint
The gateway makes no outbound call to a destination outside the configured allowlist
Gateway credentials are short lived, audience bound and rotated independently of user provider keys
observability: Publishes request counts, reconciliation mismatches and key decryption events without content
Publishes rejected workload identity, delegated-subject failure and provider-key revocation counts without key material
tests: External reachability test
Log scan test with a planted key
Streaming reconciliation exactness test
Cross-user context bleed attempts
Plan change propagation test
Forged and wrong-audience service identity tests
Provider-key replacement, cache invalidation and revocation tests
Step-up freshness, recovery suspension, cooling-off and verified-notification tests
rollout_rollback: Deployed disabled; enabling requires the egress policy to be in place and verified
Rollback disables the gateway, which disables all model features cleanly
non_goals: Custom endpoint support, which is a separate ticket
Product features, which belong to E18
Production enablement of paid traffic, which stays gated on the billing implementation; development and test run against the published quota contract and its mock

items.title: Enforce egress policy denying private, loopback, link-local and metadata destinations
items.outcome: At the network layer, the AI workload cannot reach private ranges, loopback, link-local addresses or the runtime metadata endpoint, so an application-layer validation bypass still fails.
items.context: The research assumed a network policy primitive from a container orchestrator that is not the chosen runtime, which left the network layer of the defence unimplemented. Application-layer validation alone has a long history of being bypassed through redirection and name resolution tricks.
scope: Egress restriction implemented with the primitives available on the chosen runtime
Denied destination classes covering private ranges, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade address space and the equivalents in the newer address family
Explicit denial of the runtime metadata endpoint

Two distinct destination classes: code-managed provider destinations held in the allowlist as code, and runtime custom destinations that a user or operator registers and that are validated and pinned before first use
Verification executed from inside the running workload rather than from a build machine
Registration, validation and pinning path for a runtime custom destination, including who may register one, what is validated at registration, and how the resolved address is pinned
acceptance_criteria: A connection attempt from inside the workload to the metadata endpoint fails at the network layer
Attempts to reach private, loopback, link-local and carrier-grade addresses all fail from inside the workload
The same attempts fail for the newer address family, not only the older one
A destination outside the provider allowlist is refused
Adding a destination requires a code change and review rather than a console action
The verification runs on a schedule so a drifted rule is detected
Egress policy is re-evaluated on every redirect hop and a redirect to a private, loopback, link-local or metadata destination is denied
The resolved address is pinned for the life of the request, and a rebinding attempt between validation and connection is denied and alerted
IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses and alternate textual encodings of denied addresses are normalised before comparison and denied
The container credential endpoint at 169.254.170.2 and the instance metadata service are denied explicitly, proven by a test that attempts both
The policy distinguishes code-managed provider destinations from runtime registered destinations, and each class states its own approval path
A code-managed provider destination can only be added by a code change and review; a console or runtime addition to that class is refused

A runtime custom destination is refused until it passes registration validation, which rejects private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade and metadata addresses in every textual encoding and in both address families
A validated runtime destination is pinned: the address resolved at registration is the address used, and a later change of resolution is denied and alerted rather than followed
A runtime destination can be revoked, and revocation takes effect on in-flight configuration within the published bound
The two classes are separately reported, so an operator can see how many runtime destinations exist without reading the code allowlist
contracts_schema: Publishes the allowlist as a machine-readable artifact referenced by the application-layer validator
security_privacy: This is the second layer; the application-layer validator is the first and neither is sufficient alone
Rule changes are audited and alert on modification
A runtime custom destination is never trusted because a user supplied it; it is validated, pinned and revocable, and it can never widen the code-managed provider allowlist
observability: Publishes denied connection counts by destination class
tests: In-workload connection attempts per denied class
Address family coverage test
Scheduled drift verification
Registration rejection test per denied address class for a runtime custom destination
Pinning test proving a post-registration resolution change is denied and alerted
Test proving a runtime destination cannot be promoted into the code-managed provider class at runtime
rollout_rollback: Applied before the gateway is enabled; the gateway stays disabled until verification is green
Rollback tightens rather than loosens; removing the policy disables the workload
non_goals: Application-layer address validation, which is a separate ticket
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo infra. Owns the network rules and verification job. The ai-service repository consumes the published allowlist.

items.title: Implement custom endpoint validation and the adversarial request-forgery suite
items.outcome: A user-supplied provider address is registered once, validated, resolved and pinned, never accepted in a request body, and an adversarial suite that actually attempts the known bypasses proves the defence works before the mode is exposed at all.
items.context: A user-supplied base address is a server-side request forgery primitive by construction. Assertions that the validator rejects a bad address prove very little; only tests that attempt name-resolution rebinding, redirection and alternate address encodings show whether the defence holds.
scope: Register-once flow with validation at registration rather than per request
Transport restricted to secure connections only
Resolution at registration with the resolved address pinned for subsequent use
Rejection of any attempt to supply an address in a request body
Re-validation on a schedule and on registration change
Fresh phishing-resistant step-up for registration or destination change
Risk-triggered twenty-four-hour pending activation with verified-channel notification and user cancellation
Immediate disablement on account recovery, credential reset or endpoint-integrity failure
Adversarial suite that attempts, rather than asserts, each known bypass
acceptance_criteria: Registering an address that resolves into a denied range is refused with a clear reason
The suite attempts the metadata endpoint, private ranges, loopback, carrier-grade space and the newer address family, and every attempt is blocked
A name-resolution rebinding attempt is blocked because the resolved address is pinned
A redirect to a denied destination is not followed
Supplying an address in a request body is rejected by the contract itself
The mode remains behind a kill switch until every suite case passes, and the switch state is auditable

A stale or absent step-up cannot register or change an endpoint; after recovery or on an untrusted device the endpoint remains pending for twenty-four hours and the user can cancel from a verified-channel notification
Account recovery, credential reset, failed re-validation or a pinned-address change disables the endpoint before another request can route
contracts_schema: The contract has no field capable of carrying a per-request base address; registration is a separate operation
security_privacy: Registration and every use are audited with the resolved address
A validation failure denies rather than falling back to a default provider
observability: Publishes registration attempts, validation failures and blocked destination counts
tests: Adversarial suite attempting each bypass class
Rebinding attempt test
Redirect following test
Contract test proving no body field can carry an address
Step-up freshness, cooling-off, notification cancellation and recovery-revocation tests
rollout_rollback: The mode stays disabled behind a kill switch until the suite is green, then enabled per cohort
Rollback flips the kill switch, which takes effect without a deploy
non_goals: Network-layer egress denial, which is the infra ticket
The decision on whether a client-direct mode exists, which is settled by the decision record

items.title: Build the deterministic tool layer that owns all AI-facing arithmetic
items.outcome: Every figure the assistant can mention comes from a deterministic, per-user-scoped tool implemented in the backend, so the model narrates numbers rather than producing them.
items.context: A confidently wrong figure destroys trust permanently, and the only structural defence is to make the model incapable of producing one. Scoping must live inside the tool rather than in the prompt, because a prompt is attacker-influenced input and a query filter is not.
scope: Tool set covering transaction queries, balances, debt schedules, goal simulation and budget status
Per-user scoping enforced inside each tool implementation, never taken from the model input
Deterministic results verified against the independent model harness
Structured results carrying the values and their provenance identifiers
Explicit refusal shape when a tool cannot answer, rather than a partial result
Workload authentication and delegated-subject verification before any deterministic tool is dispatched
acceptance_criteria: Every tool enforces the caller's user scope internally and ignores any scope supplied in its arguments, proven by an attempted cross-user call
Tool results agree with the independent model across the full case matrix
A tool that cannot answer returns an explicit refusal rather than an empty or approximate result
Results are reproducible: the same inputs produce the same values and provenance identifiers
No tool performs a write; the tool layer is read-only
Every tool call is audited with the tool name and scope, without arguments containing personal data
A forged, expired, replayed or widened delegated subject is rejected before a ledger query executes
Tool payloads carry money as the canonical decimal string with its currency and are parsed into the Decimal-backed Python wrapper, never as a float
contracts_schema: Implements the published tool contract in which the user scope is a required, server-derived parameter
security_privacy: Tools are the isolation boundary for the AI subsystem; a compromised model cannot widen its own scope
Tool output carries no counterparty text beyond the stated policy
Tool implementations receive a verified internal subject object rather than a user identifier from model or request arguments
observability: Publishes tool call counts, refusal counts and latency per tool
tests: Cross-user scope attempt tests per tool
Independent model agreement tests
Determinism tests
Read-only assertion test
Forged, expired, replayed and widened delegated-subject rejection tests per tool group
rollout_rollback: Shipped before any model feature; the assistant cannot be enabled without it
Rollback disables the tool endpoints, which disables the assistant
non_goals: Prompt construction and model routing, which the ai-service tickets own
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the tool implementations. The ai-service repository calls them through the published contract and implements no arithmetic of its own.

items.title: Implement the tool dispatcher, injection defences and data minimisation
items.outcome: Only allowlisted tools can be invoked, ingested text is treated as hostile data rather than instructions, and identifying details are minimised before any external call without altering the figures an answer cites.
items.context: Merchant names and transaction notes are attacker-controlled input that arrives from outside and ends up near a model, which is the textbook injection path. This ticket is the runtime boundary; the evaluation and spend gates that police its output are a separate ticket with a different failure mode.
scope: Allowlist dispatcher rejecting any unknown tool name, with no dynamic registration
Ingested content passed only as data, never inside instructions, with encoding that prevents instruction confusion
Screening for suspected injection with a defined response and an abuse counter
Minimisation of identifying details before any external call, without altering the figures that answers cite
Trace redaction so no key or raw counterparty string is retained beyond policy
No persisted embedding of user-derived transaction, merchant, memo or assistant text until T-ADR-EMBED-12 is accepted and its storage and erasure controls are implemented
acceptance_criteria: An unknown tool name is rejected and recorded rather than attempted
A hostile merchant name cannot induce a tool call the user did not ask for, proven by an adversarial corpus
No ingested text appears inside the instruction portion of any request, proven by an outbound payload inspection test
Minimisation never rounds or alters an amount that an answer will cite, proven by a fidelity test
Traces contain no key material and no raw counterparty strings beyond policy
A schema and migration gate rejects pgvector, another vector extension or a user-derived embedding column while T-ADR-EMBED-12 remains open
contracts_schema: Consumes the published tool contract; the dispatcher cannot call anything absent from it
security_privacy: Injection screening results are recorded without storing the hostile content verbatim in an unbounded way
Data minimisation is applied before egress, not after logging
observability: Publishes injection suspicion counts, dispatcher rejections and minimisation coverage
tests: Unknown tool rejection test
Adversarial injection corpus in continuous integration
Outbound payload inspection test
Numeric fidelity zero-tolerance test on the minimisation path
rollout_rollback: Dispatcher and defences ship together; the gateway cannot be enabled without them
Rollback lowers the routing tier rather than removing the injection defences
non_goals: Evaluation gating and spend controls, which are their own ticket
Product features, which belong to E18
Quota accounting, which the billing ticket owns
Persisted transaction or conversation embeddings, which require T-ADR-EMBED-12 and a separately reviewed implementation ticket

items.title: Gate AI merges on the evaluation suite, numeric fidelity and spend controls
items.outcome: An evaluation suite blocks merges on accuracy or numeric-fidelity regression, and cost anomalies trip a kill switch that stops traffic rather than sending an email.
items.context: Cost is the structural risk the runtime boundary does not address: without a hard stop, a single loop can consume a month of margin overnight. Evaluation is the other: a model change that quietly degrades categorisation is invisible until users report it.
scope: Evaluation suite covering categorisation accuracy, adversarial cases and numeric fidelity, blocking merges
Numeric fidelity cases treated as zero tolerance rather than as a scored metric
Cost anomaly detection with per-user throttling and a global kill switch that stops traffic
Published baseline so a regression is measured against a recorded number rather than an impression
Governed evaluation corpus with a named owner, recorded provenance per case and a change process
Provider model and version pinning, with an evaluation rerun forced by any version change
Harmful-answer incident path: report, containment, correction and its relationship to the kill switch and the on-call rota
acceptance_criteria: The evaluation suite fails a merge when accuracy drops below the threshold or any numeric fidelity case fails
Exceeding the global spend cap stops traffic rather than only alerting, verified in a test environment
Per-user throttling engages before the global cap and is recorded
The baseline is published and a change to it is a reviewed change rather than a silent one
The evaluation suite fails a merge when task accuracy falls below 95 percent on the governed corpus
The governed corpus contains at least 1000 synthetic cases with recorded provenance, plus at least 50 adversarial cases, and a case with no recorded provenance is invalid
The corpus has a named owner, and adding, changing or removing a case is a reviewed change rather than an edit
Every provider model is pinned to an explicit version, and an unpinned model reference fails the build
Changing a pinned model version forces a full evaluation rerun before that version can serve traffic, proven by a test that changes a version and asserts the gate

A harmful answer has a defined path: it can be reported from the product, it is contained by disabling the affected capability or tripping the kill switch, a correction is issued, and the on-call rota is named as the responder
A reported harmful answer is added to the adversarial case set as part of its correction, so the same failure cannot silently return
contracts_schema: Evaluation results and spend counters are published in a documented shape that the release checklist reads
security_privacy: Evaluation fixtures are synthetic; no production content is used as an evaluation case
Spend counters carry no request content
The governed corpus is synthetic; no real user content enters it, and a reported harmful answer is de-identified before it becomes a case
The kill switch is reachable by the on-call responder without a deployment
observability: Publishes evaluation scores, spend against cap, throttle activations and kill switch events
Harmful-answer reports, containment actions and corrections are counted and dated, so a rising rate is visible before it is anecdotal
tests: Evaluation gate test with a planted accuracy regression
Numeric fidelity zero-tolerance test
Spend cap enforcement test
Throttle activation test
Accuracy floor enforcement test at the 95 percent boundary
Corpus size and provenance validation test
Unpinned model reference build failure test
Version-change forces rerun test
Harmful-answer containment drill exercising the kill switch and the on-call path
rollout_rollback: Evaluation gate introduced as reporting for one release to establish the baseline, then blocking
Rollback returns the gate to reporting; the spend kill switch is never rolled back
non_goals: Dispatcher and injection defences, which are their own ticket
Product features, which belong to E18

items.title: Implement bounded provider routing, failover and circuit breakers for the AI gateway
items.outcome: The gateway routes only across an allowlisted set of provider, region and model combinations approved for zero data retention, trips a circuit breaker on sustained provider failure, retries and fails over while consuming exactly the quota that was reserved, and returns an explicit all-providers-unavailable state rather than a generic error or a silent retry loop.
items.context: T-AI-01 built the gateway, its virtual keys and the metering bridge, and T-AI-06 gates merges on evaluation and spend, but neither defines what happens when a provider is slow, down or outside its permitted region. An uncontrolled retry can double-count reserved quota or route a request to a destination the egress policy never approved.
scope: Provider routing bounded to an allowlist of provider, region and model combinations approved for zero data retention
Circuit breaker per provider that opens on sustained failure and half-opens after a cooldown
Retry and failover logic that consumes exactly one reservation's worth of quota regardless of how many providers are attempted
Explicit all-providers-unavailable response distinct from a single-provider failure
Routing decision recorded for every request for audit
acceptance_criteria: A request never reaches a provider, region or model outside the allowlist, proven by an attempted disallowed route
An open circuit stops new requests to a failing provider until its cooldown elapses
A failover across three simulated provider failures still consumes only one reservation's worth of quota
When every allowlisted provider is unavailable, the caller receives the explicit all-providers-unavailable state rather than a generic error or an unbounded retry loop
Every routing decision is recorded with the provider chosen and its outcome
contracts_schema: Consumes the published quota contract for exactly-once reservation semantics; the routing table itself is internal gateway configuration, not part of the public contract
security_privacy: The allowlist is the sole source of truth for permitted destinations, and a change to it is reviewed as a security change
Circuit breaker and routing telemetry carries no request content
observability: Publishes routing decisions by provider and outcome, circuit breaker state transitions, quota-exact retry counts and all-providers-unavailable occurrences
tests: Disallowed-route rejection test
Circuit breaker open and cooldown test
Quota-exact failover test across simulated multi-provider failure
All-providers-unavailable explicit-state test
rollout_rollback: Enabled behind a flag with a single provider first; additional providers and failover are added one at a time
Rollback pins routing to the last known-good single provider and disables failover rather than removing the gateway
non_goals: The gateway's key storage and metering bridge, which T-AI-01 owns
Evaluation gating and spend controls, which T-AI-06 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo ai-service. Owns the routing table, circuit breakers and failover logic. Quota reservation itself remains owned by the api repository's published contract.
